domain_label: Hierarchical & Recursive Task Decomposition (Recursive Planning Engine subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the decomposition method itself; termination proofs and contract composition are delegated to sibling KBs
a world/state model and an operator catalog are available to ground primitives
tasks carry type signatures from which arity and method applicability are derived
exclusions: interface contracts and assume/guarantee composition (delegated to contract__composition_failure)
operator implementation internals and runtime execution

competency_questions.question: How is the root goal captured and typed, and what is its success criterion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOAL_INTAKE and TASK_TYPING define goal typing and success criterion

competency_questions.question: What decomposition methods exist and how are they catalogued?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METHOD_LIBRARY defines the catalog and applicability conditions

competency_questions.question: How is a method selected among applicable alternatives, and how does selection recover on dead-ends?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METHOD_SELECT ranks applicable methods; ALT_METHOD_BACKTRACK recovers

competency_questions.question: How is subtask arity determined and checked from a task's type?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARITY_TYPING derives the required subtask set from the type signature

competency_questions.question: How are method preconditions verified before expansion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRECOND_CHECK evaluates preconditions against fresh state

competency_questions.question: How are concrete subtasks instantiated from a chosen method?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBTASK_EMIT instantiates typed child tasks with provenance

competency_questions.question: How is the decomposition kept acyclic and how is shared-subtask reuse handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECOMP_DAG maintains the acyclic refinement graph

competency_questions.question: How are subtasks ordered, causal links protected, and parameters bound?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORDERING_CONSTRAINTS and PARAM_BINDING establish the partial order and bindings

competency_questions.question: How are constraints propagated and conflicts/clobbers detected across levels?
What is the core refinement loop and how does it ground primitives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFINE_LOOP expands to primitives; PRIMITIVE_GROUNDING binds operators

competency_questions.question: How is decomposition depth/breadth bounded, what happens on budget exhaustion, and how does it interface with termination?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECOMP_DEPTH_BUDGET bounds expansion and raises defeaters

competency_questions.question: How does the planner recover: backtracking versus bounded local repair?
How is each primitive leaf grounded, verified executable, and its provenance recorded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRIMITIVE_GROUNDING grounds; LEAF_VERIFICATION closes open conditions; DECOMP_TRACE records provenance

competency_questions.question: How is full goal coverage and scope containment verified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_CHECK verifies set-cover closure and that no leaf is out of scope

glossary.definition: a task that is not directly executable and must be expanded by a method into subtasks
a task directly executable by a single grounded operator/action
a named expansion of a compound task type into a typed subtask set with preconditions
the acyclic graph of tasks and refinement edges produced during decomposition
a producer->consumer protection between two subtasks over a condition
a subtask precondition not yet established by another subtask's effect
when a subtask's effect deletes a condition another subtask depends on
a recorded decision with untried alternatives used as a backtracking target
the property that every goal obligation is covered by at least one leaf

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for hierarchical task decomposition work units, informed by classical HTN planning (Erol/Hendler/Nau SHOP/SHOP2), partial-order causal-link planning (UCPOP), and least-commitment planning; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Erol, Hendler & Nau 1994 HTN Planning; Nau et al. 2003 SHOP2; Weld 1994 An Introduction to Least-Commitment Planning; Ghallab, Nau & Traverso 2004 Automated Planning

nodes.definition: Capture the root goal/task and attach a type signature, success criterion, and the world/state model the decomposition will refine against.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: goal grammar or success-criterion definition changes

pros.claim: A typed, criterion-bearing goal makes every later refinement checkable against a fixed target
pros.example: goal 'ship release' typed as compound with acceptance = all gates green

cons.claim: Premature goal typing can over-constrain decomposition before the space is understood
cons.example: typing a research goal as a fixed pipeline hides exploratory subgoals

failure_modes: untyped goal admits no termination or coverage check
acceptance_tests: goal has an explicit type and machine-checkable success criterion

nodes.definition: Maintain the catalog of decomposition methods: for each compound task type, the alternative expansions (subtask templates) with their preconditions and applicability conditions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new task type added or a method's preconditions change

pros.claim: A first-class method library separates 'what expansions exist' from 'which to pick now', enabling reuse and audit
pros.example: one 'deploy' type with three methods: blue-green, canary, rolling

cons.claim: Library drift: stale methods whose preconditions no longer match the world model
cons.example: a method assumes a tool that was removed

failure_modes: unindexed methods cause exponential selection cost
duplicate methods with subtly different preconditions
acceptance_tests: every compound type has at least one applicable method indexed by type

nodes.definition: Classify each task node as primitive (directly executable) or compound (must be expanded), and assign its type signature so arity and method selection are determined by type.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: type system or primitive/compound boundary redefined

pros.claim: Type-driven typing makes decomposition obligations explicit and lets arity be checked, not guessed
pros.example: a 'transfer' type fixes exactly {debit, credit, reconcile} subtasks

cons.claim: A coarse type system forces unnatural classifications
cons.example: binary primitive/compound hides 'semi-primitive' tasks needing a tool call

failure_modes: mis-typing a compound as primitive yields an unexecutable leaf
type signature too loose to constrain arity
acceptance_tests: each task carries a resolved type; no leaf is left untyped

nodes.definition: Derive the number and types of subtasks a compound task must produce from its type signature, so decomposition arity is a checkable obligation rather than an ad hoc choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a task type's required subtask set is revised

pros.claim: Arity-as-obligation catches under-decomposition (a missing required subtask) deterministically
pros.example: 'transfer' missing 'reconcile' fails arity check before execution

cons.claim: Strict arity rejects legitimate variability when a type genuinely has variable fan-out
cons.example: aggregating an unknown number of shards

acceptance_tests: arity obligations satisfied for every compound node

nodes.definition: Select among the methods applicable to a compound task given current preconditions; rank by cost/confidence and record the choice plus the unselected alternatives for backtracking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: selection policy or cost model changes

pros.claim: Recording unselected alternatives turns method choice into a recoverable decision, not a commit
pros.example: keep canary as fallback when blue-green is selected

cons.claim: Greedy selection by local cost can pick a method that dead-ends deeper in the tree
cons.example: cheapest expansion needs an unavailable resource two levels down

acceptance_tests: at least one applicable method selected or an explicit no-method defeater is raised
revisit_triggers: new method added to a type
downstream dead-ends traced to a selection

nodes.definition: Verify a candidate method's preconditions against the current world/state model before expansion, so methods are only applied where their assumptions hold.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: world-model schema or precondition language changes

pros.claim: Checking preconditions before expansion prevents committing to infeasible subtrees
pros.example: skip canary method when no traffic-splitter exists

cons.claim: Precondition checks are only as good as the world model; stale state yields false applicability
cons.example: model says service is up but it is mid-restart

acceptance_tests: preconditions evaluate true against a freshly read state before expansion

nodes.definition: Instantiate the chosen method into concrete subtasks: create child task nodes, carry over parameters, and attach their type signatures and obligations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: subtask instantiation contract changes

pros.claim: Explicit instantiation makes the refinement step a typed, inspectable artifact
pros.example: each child records which method and binding produced it

cons.claim: Instantiation without provenance makes later repair and audit impossible
cons.example: a child appears with no link to its parent method

acceptance_tests: each emitted subtask is typed and linked to its generating method

nodes.definition: Maintain the decomposition as an acyclic refinement graph (tree/DAG): nodes are tasks, edges are refinement links; enforce that no task refines (transitively) into itself.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: refinement-graph invariants change

pros.claim: An explicit acyclic refinement graph makes recursion safe and enables shared-subtask reuse
pros.example: two parents share one 'build-image' subtask without duplication

cons.claim: DAG reuse complicates ownership and parameter binding of shared subtasks
cons.example: shared subtask needs different parameters per parent

failure_modes: a refinement cycle (task expands into itself)
acceptance_tests: refinement graph is acyclic at every step
shared subtasks are reused not duplicated
revisit_triggers: a cycle is detected in staging

nodes.definition: Establish partial-order and causal-link constraints among subtasks (before/after, producer/consumer) so the decomposition is a partial order, not an over-committed total order.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ordering semantics or causal-link policy changes

pros.claim: Least-commitment partial order preserves parallelism and avoids premature sequencing
pros.example: two independent subtasks left unordered run concurrently downstream

cons.claim: Causal-link bookkeeping (threats/promotion/demotion) is intricate and error-prone
cons.example: a new subtask threatens an existing producer-consumer link

failure_modes: over-commitment to a total order kills parallelism
unprotected causal link clobbered by a later effect
acceptance_tests: ordering is a consistent partial order with all causal links protected
revisit_triggers: a clobbered link traced in execution

nodes.definition: Bind variables and unify parameters across subtasks so outputs of one subtask flow as typed inputs to another, maintaining a consistent substitution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: binding/type-unification rules change

pros.claim: Unification gives a single consistent substitution, catching type-incompatible dataflow early
pros.example: binding a string output into an int-typed input fails at bind time

cons.claim: Aggressive early binding can over-constrain when a value is genuinely deferred
cons.example: binding a region before the cost-optimizer has chosen one

failure_modes: late binding hides a type error until execution
acceptance_tests: all bound parameters are type-consistent under one substitution
revisit_triggers: a binding type error reaches execution

nodes.definition: Propagate constraints up and down the decomposition (preconditions, resource limits, deadlines) so that a constraint introduced at one level is enforced across the affected subtree.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: constraint language or propagation rules change

pros.claim: Propagation makes a parent-level deadline bind every descendant automatically
pros.example: a 5-minute budget at the root caps the sum of leaf budgets

cons.claim: Propagation can over-tighten and make a satisfiable decomposition look infeasible
cons.example: conservative interval arithmetic rejects a feasible schedule

failure_modes: constraint added at one level not enforced at another
acceptance_tests: constraints are consistent across the affected subtree after propagation
revisit_triggers: an unpropagated constraint causes a late failure

nodes.definition: Iteratively expand compound leaves until every leaf is primitive, interleaving method selection and precondition checks; this is the core recursive loop and must make monotonic progress.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: refinement/termination interface changes

pros.claim: A single refinement loop with a progress measure localizes all recursion in one auditable place
pros.example: loop exits when |compound leaves| reaches 0

cons.claim: Without a ranking/measure the loop can expand forever on recursive task types
cons.example: 'simplify' that re-emits a 'simplify' subtask

acceptance_tests: refinement terminates with all leaves primitive on every test goal
revisit_triggers: a runaway expansion observed in staging

nodes.definition: Bound decomposition depth and per-node breadth (fan-out) and expose the bound to the termination layer, so unbounded or explosive expansion is caught as a defeater, not a crash.

excluded: proof of termination (delegated to termination KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: depth/breadth budget policy changes

pros.claim: An explicit budget converts silent blow-up into an explicit, handleable defeater
pros.example: depth>12 raises a budget defeater routed to repair

cons.claim: A fixed budget can truncate a legitimately deep decomposition
cons.example: a genuinely 15-level task is cut at 12

failure_modes: budget too low truncates valid plans
budget too high lets blow-up run long before tripping
acceptance_tests: every expansion path is bounded by an explicit depth and breadth budget
revisit_triggers: truncation of a valid plan observed

nodes.definition: Detect inconsistencies across the decomposition: contradictory subgoals, resource clobbering, and mutually exclusive method choices, before they reach execution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: conflict taxonomy or detection method changes

pros.claim: Detecting clobbering at decomposition time is far cheaper than at execution time
pros.example: two subtasks both claim an exclusive lock are flagged pre-run

cons.claim: Detection sensitivity trades false positives against missed conflicts
cons.example: semantic contradictions that are lexically dissimilar slip through

acceptance_tests: all resource clobbers and contradictory subgoals are detected before execution

nodes.definition: On a detected dead-end or conflict, backtrack to the nearest decision with an untried alternative method and re-expand, rather than restarting the whole decomposition.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: backtracking policy or choice-point recording changes

pros.claim: Chronological/dependency-directed backtracking reuses the valid prefix instead of discarding it
pros.example: conflict at depth 6 re-tries the depth-5 method, keeping depths 0-4

cons.claim: Naive backtracking can thrash between two failing alternatives without progress
cons.example: two methods alternately tried, both dead-ending

failure_modes: backtrack target chosen too shallow or too deep
acceptance_tests: backtracking reaches a consistent decomposition or exhausts alternatives with an explicit failure

nodes.definition: Repair a partial decomposition locally (replace a failing subtree, re-bind, re-order) instead of backtracking or restarting, when the failure is contained.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repair scope or locality criteria change

pros.claim: Local repair preserves most of the decomposition and converges faster than restart when failure is contained
pros.example: swap one failing leaf's method, keep the rest

cons.claim: Repair can mask a structural problem that really needs backtracking
cons.example: patching leaves repeatedly around a wrong high-level method

failure_modes: repair masks a need for structural backtrack
acceptance_tests: repair restores consistency or escalates to backtracking after a bounded number of attempts

nodes.definition: Bind each primitive leaf to an executable operator/action with its concrete parameters and verify the operator's signature matches the leaf's type.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: operator catalog or grounding contract changes

pros.claim: Grounding with signature checks guarantees every leaf is actually executable
pros.example: a 'send-email' leaf binds to an operator with matching typed params

cons.claim: A missing operator for a typed leaf reveals a gap that decomposition alone cannot fix
cons.example: no operator exists for a required primitive

failure_modes: leaf bound to a signature-mismatched operator
acceptance_tests: every primitive leaf binds to a signature-matching executable operator

nodes.definition: Verify that the set of grounded leaves is collectively executable and that each leaf's preconditions are establishable by the partial order, closing open conditions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: executability criteria change

pros.claim: Closing open conditions before execution turns 'looks done' into 'provably executable'
pros.example: each leaf precondition is established by an earlier leaf's effect

cons.claim: Establishment proofs assume the world model is complete; unmodeled effects break them
cons.example: an external actor changes state between plan and run

acceptance_tests: no open preconditions remain; the grounded leaf set is collectively executable
revisit_triggers: an unestablished precondition failed at runtime

nodes.definition: Record the full provenance of the decomposition: for each node, the parent task, chosen method, binding, and the alternatives not taken, for audit, explanation, and repair.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: provenance schema changes

pros.claim: A provenance trace makes the decomposition explainable and makes repair/backtracking precise
pros.example: 'why this subtask?' answered by parent+method+binding

cons.claim: Full provenance adds storage and write overhead proportional to tree size
cons.example: a deep tree logs thousands of choice records

acceptance_tests: every node carries parent, method, binding and unselected-alternative provenance
revisit_triggers: a repair failed for lack of provenance

nodes.definition: Verify that the decomposition fully covers the root goal's success criterion: every obligation maps to at least one leaf, and no leaf is outside the goal's scope (set-cover closure).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: goal-coverage definition changes

pros.claim: Set-cover closure makes 'the plan achieves the goal' a checkable property, not a hope
pros.example: each success-criterion clause is covered by >=1 leaf

cons.claim: Coverage over the modeled criterion can still miss an unstated real-world obligation
cons.example: criterion omits a compliance step that matters

acceptance_tests: every success-criterion obligation is covered and no leaf is out of scope

edges.why_related: budget defeater feeds back to halt/redirect the refinement loop
backtracking re-invokes selection at a prior choice point
causal links are the objects whose threats CONFLICT_DETECT checks
arity obligations are part of the coverage obligation set
provenance supplies the choice points backtracking targets
provenance localizes the subtree repair replaces
greedy least-cost method selection conflicts with global refinement feasibility
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: prefer downstream-feasible methods: when greedy local selection dead-ends, REFINE_LOOP's failure backpropagates to re-rank selection by realized feasibility

edges.why_related: a tight depth budget can truncate decomposition before full goal coverage is reached
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: raise the depth budget only when COVERAGE_CHECK proves the truncated obligations are real; otherwise treat truncation as a defeater not a coverage failure

edges.why_related: eager ordering during refinement reduces the parallelism least-commitment aims to preserve
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: least-commitment: keep subtasks unordered during refinement and add ordering only when a threat is detected, not eagerly

edges.why_related: local repair and backtracking compete as recovery strategies for the same failure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: try bounded local repair first; escalate to backtracking when repair attempts exceed the bound without restoring consistency

conflict_axes.name: least_commitment_vs_eager_ordering
conflict_axes.description: Deferring ordering preserves parallelism but complicates threat tracking; eager ordering simplifies reasoning but over-commits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add ordering only to resolve a detected threat

conflict_axes.name: greedy_local_selection_vs_global_feasibility
conflict_axes.description: Greedy method selection is cheap but can dead-end deep in the tree where a globally better method was available.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record alternatives; backpropagate refinement failure to re-rank

conflict_axes.name: depth_budget_vs_goal_coverage
conflict_axes.description: A tight depth/breadth budget bounds cost but can truncate before full coverage; a loose budget risks blow-up.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat truncation as a defeater; raise budget only against proven real obligations

conflict_axes.name: backtracking_vs_local_repair
conflict_axes.description: Backtracking is sound but can discard valid work; local repair is fast but can mask structural errors.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bounded repair first, then escalate to backtracking

conflict_axes.name: early_binding_vs_deferred_binding
conflict_axes.description: Early parameter binding catches type errors sooner but over-constrains genuinely deferred values.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bind when a type or causal link forces it; otherwise defer

conflict_axes.name: fixed_arity_vs_variable_fanout
conflict_axes.description: Type-fixed arity catches under-decomposition but rejects legitimate data-dependent fan-out.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model variable fan-out as a typed collection task with its own arity rule

conflict_axes.name: shared_subtask_reuse_vs_binding_isolation
conflict_axes.description: DAG reuse of a shared subtask saves work but entangles per-parent parameter binding.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reuse structure but clone binding context per parent

conflict_axes.name: provenance_completeness_vs_overhead
conflict_axes.description: Full provenance enables precise repair and explanation but costs storage proportional to tree size.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record decisions and alternatives; sample verbose intermediate state

conflict_axes.name: world_model_trust_vs_recheck_cost
conflict_axes.description: Trusting the world model speeds precondition checks but risks acting on stale state.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-read volatile conditions just before expansion and execution

edge_cases.description: Recursive task type re-emits itself, producing an infinite refinement chain.
edge_cases.trigger: a method expands a compound task into a subtask of the same type with no progress measure
edge_cases.mitigation: require a strictly decreasing progress measure; depth budget raises a defeater

edge_cases.description: A required subtask is silently missing, so the plan looks complete but cannot achieve the goal.
edge_cases.trigger: arity obligation not enforced for a compound task
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce type-driven arity; coverage check maps obligations to leaves

edge_cases.description: Two subtasks clobber a shared resource detected only at execution.
edge_cases.trigger: causal-link threat not checked at decomposition time
edge_cases.mitigation: detect clobbering during decomposition; protect links by promotion/demotion

edge_cases.description: Greedy method selection dead-ends at depth and the planner restarts from scratch, discarding valid work.
edge_cases.trigger: no choice points recorded for backtracking
edge_cases.mitigation: record alternatives at each selection; backtrack to nearest untried alternative

edge_cases.description: Depth budget truncates a legitimately deep decomposition, dropping real obligations.
edge_cases.trigger: budget set below the true required depth
edge_cases.mitigation: raise budget only when coverage proves the truncated obligations are real

edge_cases.description: A primitive leaf has no matching operator, so the plan is unexecutable.
edge_cases.trigger: operator catalog lacks an operator for a typed leaf
edge_cases.mitigation: signature-match grounding; raise a gap defeater when no operator exists

edge_cases.description: Local repair loops indefinitely, patching leaves around a wrong high-level method.
edge_cases.trigger: repair attempts exceed bound without restoring consistency
edge_cases.mitigation: bound repair attempts; escalate to backtracking the higher method

edge_cases.description: Stale world model makes a precondition look satisfied; expansion commits to an infeasible subtree.
edge_cases.mitigation: re-read volatile conditions immediately before expansion

edge_cases.description: Eager total ordering during refinement removes parallelism the plan needed to meet a deadline.
edge_cases.trigger: ordering added before any threat required it
edge_cases.mitigation: least-commitment ordering: add constraints only on detected threats

edge_cases.description: Shared (reused) subtask receives conflicting parameter bindings from two parents.
edge_cases.trigger: DAG reuse without per-parent binding context
edge_cases.mitigation: clone binding context per parent while sharing structure

edge_cases.description: An open precondition is left unestablished and fails at runtime.
edge_cases.trigger: leaf verification skipped for a closed-world assumption
edge_cases.mitigation: close all open conditions before execution; mark unmodeled effects

edge_cases.description: Provenance is absent, so a failed leaf cannot be repaired without a full restart.

workflow.description: Capture the root goal, attach a type and machine-checkable success criterion, and load the world model.
workflow.gate: goal has a type and success criterion

workflow.description: Ensure every compound type has at least one applicable, precondition-annotated method indexed.
workflow.gate: each compound type has >=1 indexed method

workflow.description: Filter to applicable methods, rank by cost/confidence, record unselected alternatives as choice points.
workflow.gate: a method is selected or a no-method defeater raised

workflow.description: Evaluate the chosen method's preconditions against freshly read state before expansion.
Create typed child tasks with provenance and satisfy the type's arity obligation.
workflow.gate: arity obligation satisfied; children carry provenance

workflow.description: Insert refinement edges and assert acyclicity; reuse shared subtasks where sound.
Add least-commitment ordering and causal links; unify parameter bindings.
workflow.gate: partial order consistent; causal links protected

workflow.description: Expand compound leaves until all are primitive, bounded by the depth/breadth budget.
workflow.gate: all leaves primitive; progress measure strictly decreased

workflow.description: Detect clobbers/contradictions; recover by bounded repair then backtracking.
Bind each primitive leaf to a signature-matching operator.
workflow.gate: every leaf bound to a matching operator

workflow.description: Close open conditions and confirm collective executability.
Confirm set-cover closure of the success criterion and scope containment.
workflow.gate: all obligations covered; no out-of-scope leaf

priority_rationale: GOAL_INTAKE/TASK_TYPING/METHOD_LIBRARY are foundational; REFINE_LOOP and DECOMP_DAG are the recursion core; CONFLICT_DETECT and recovery gate correctness; verification and coverage close the method last.

dominance_rules.rule: GOAL_INTAKE typing and success criterion must be fixed before METHOD_SELECT runs
dominance_rules.rationale: selection and arity are derived from the goal type; selecting first causes rework
dominance_rules.trigger: method selection begins without a typed goal
dominance_rules.action: block until the goal has a type and success criterion

dominance_rules.rule: REFINE_LOOP must carry a strictly decreasing progress measure or a depth budget before any cyclic task type is expanded
dominance_rules.rationale: recursive task types without a measure cause non-termination
dominance_rules.trigger: a self-recursive task type is expanded
dominance_rules.action: require a progress measure or budget defeater on the loop

dominance_rules.rule: CONFLICT_DETECT must run before PRIMITIVE_GROUNDING commits operators
dominance_rules.rationale: clobbers are far cheaper to fix at decomposition time than at execution
dominance_rules.action: block grounding until conflicts are resolved

dominance_rules.rule: ARITY_TYPING obligations must be satisfied before COVERAGE_CHECK can pass
dominance_rules.rationale: a missing required subtask is an uncovered obligation
dominance_rules.trigger: coverage check on a node with unmet arity
dominance_rules.action: fail coverage and route to SUBTASK_EMIT

dominance_rules.rule: METHOD_SELECT must record unselected alternatives before expansion
dominance_rules.rationale: backtracking needs choice points; unrecorded alternatives force a full restart

dominance_rules.rule: PRECOND_CHECK must read volatile conditions fresh immediately before expansion
dominance_rules.rationale: stale state causes commitment to infeasible subtrees
dominance_rules.action: force a fresh read of volatile conditions

dominance_rules.rule: PARTIAL_PLAN_REPAIR attempts must be bounded before escalation to ALT_METHOD_BACKTRACK
dominance_rules.action: escalate to backtracking the higher method

dominance_rules.rule: LEAF_VERIFICATION must close all open conditions before execution is permitted
dominance_rules.action: block execution until conditions are closed

dominance_rules.rule: DECOMP_DAG acyclicity invariant must hold after every refinement step
dominance_rules.rationale: a refinement cycle is non-terminating recursion
dominance_rules.trigger: a refinement edge would create a cycle
dominance_rules.action: reject the edge and raise a defeater

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select methods before the goal is typed; type changes invalidate selection
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-selecting all methods after a late goal re-typing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not expand recursive task types without a progress measure; adding one after blow-up requires reworking the loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency loop-guard retrofit on a runaway decomposition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not ground operators before conflict detection; clobbers found post-grounding require regrounding
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regrounding leaves after execution-time clobber discovery

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not eagerly totally-order subtasks; removing spurious ordering later is costly
Do not discard choice points during selection; reconstructing them for backtracking is expensive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full restart when a deep dead-end has no recorded alternatives

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not reuse a shared subtask without per-parent binding context; untangling it later requires a graph edit
Do not skip provenance recording; retrofitting it for repair requires re-running decomposition
anti_rework_rules.prevents: blind repair with no parent/method/binding trace

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not set the depth budget without coverage feedback; truncation surfaces as missing obligations late
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-planning after late discovery of truncated obligations

iteration_protocol.trigger: refinement fails to terminate or progress measure stalls
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the depth/breadth budget in DECOMP_DEPTH_BUDGET and audit recursive methods in REFINE_LOOP
extend the conflict taxonomy in CONFLICT_DETECT and add link protection in ORDERING_CONSTRAINTS

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deep dead-end causes a full restart
iteration_protocol.action: verify choice points are recorded in METHOD_SELECT and reachable by ALT_METHOD_BACKTRACK

iteration_protocol.trigger: coverage check finds an uncovered obligation
iteration_protocol.action: re-run ARITY_TYPING and SUBTASK_EMIT for the affected node

iteration_protocol.trigger: a primitive leaf has no operator
iteration_protocol.action: file an operator gap and add the operator before grounding in PRIMITIVE_GROUNDING
lower the repair bound in PARTIAL_PLAN_REPAIR and escalate to ALT_METHOD_BACKTRACK

iteration_protocol.trigger: a stale-state false applicability is observed
iteration_protocol.action: tighten volatile-condition freshness in PRECOND_CHECK and re-check in LEAF_VERIFICATION

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
